messages:
elaine: Heads up — discovered a potential cross-tenant exposure in the embeddings service after yesterday's model rollout. Seen some rows tagged with wrong tenant id. severity=high.
tom: ack. can you paste a sample log line or entry?
elaine: here's one (sanitized):
```
audit.log timestamp=1719123000 user=marta action=write resource=embeddings tenant=demo-123 produced_for=prod-789 key_id=projects/redwood/keystore/keys/kr-29
```
marta: that entry is from a support replay backfill — I ran job 8931 for demo-123 but it should not have written produced_for=prod-789. I also kicked a purge earlier this week.
raj: could be a KMS alias swap or IAM permission bleed. if decrypt worked with wrong key, metadata might have been remapped. which key id was used for the replay?
tom: checking KMS audit now. rotation was attempted 1719100000 on key kr-29, and I see the alias moved. service-account svc-embed-writer still has `roles/cloudkms.admin` in one project — that gives decrypt abilities across aliases. that's not intended.
nina: legal note — if PII crossed tenants we might need to treat this as a DSAR/incident. please pause irreversible deletes until scope is confirmed and forensics captures evidence. also check if any retention exceptions or legal holds exist for Acme/demo-123.
elaine: creating tracking ticket RDW-6372. proposed containment: 1) revoke svc-embed-writer decrypt perms 2) snapshot current embeddings + export wrapped with a sealed KMS key 3) freeze scheduled purge for affected tenants 4) prepare DSAR/notification pack.
tom: revoking now — running IAM change (will post confirmation).
```
# example
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member=serviceAccount:svc-embed-writer@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.admin
```
tom: done. svc-embed-writer decrypt revoked. starting export to gs://redwood-forensics/rdw-6372/171912 with encryption key kr-29-sealed.
sre-ops-bot: Deploy bot: rollback model rollout v2.1 -> v2.0 triggered by @tom.
marta: support artifact: replay job 8931 logs and manifest saved to /artifacts/replay-8931.tar.gz, linking to RDW-6372.
raj: for eventual safe erasure we need an audit-proof delete flow: only role `privacy_deleter` can delete embeddings, deletion requires dual-signoff (legal+sec), and proof-of-delete must be recorded as a signed JSON: `delete_proof:{deleted_by, ts, checksum, kms_key}`.
nina: legal approves preservation-first approach. create a retention exception for demo-123 until forensics clears it. we need subject lists if DSARs come in; privacy@redwood.com will coordinate.
elaine: agreed. I'll tag RDW-6372 with `retention-exception` and `forensics-hold` and add the triage notes.
tom: also disabled scheduled jobs for tenant demo-123: config `scheduling.enabled=false` set in tenant config store.
marta: small ask — when we run the safe-delete, please run a dry-run first and attach the proof JSON to the ticket.
raj: dry-run command I used for validation: 
```
python tools/purge_embeddings.py --tenant demo-123 --dry-run --output proofs/rdw-6372-dryrun.json
```
elaine: Nina — can you confirm legal hold wording in RDW-6372 and list required approvals for delete?
nina: confirmed: legal hold ON for demo-123. do NOT delete until explicit clearance from legal + sec. forward any subject requests to privacy@redwood.com. we'll prepare DSAR timeline template.
elaine: perfect. next steps: forensics export verification, RBAC hardening (remove cloudkms.admin from service accounts), create `privacy_deleter` role + process, add proof-of-delete schema to ops playbook, and evaluate retention exception window. moving this thread to incidents channel when we have a completed triage summary.
tom: ETA for forensics export verification ~2 hours.
raj: I'll draft RBAC doc and proof-of-delete schema, and prepare a script to generate signed proofs using our signing key.
marta: support will prepare customer comms if needed.
elaine: thanks team. let's avoid unilateral deletes. :thumbsup:
